clinicalPearls: Caused by de novo variants in KAT6A (also called MYST3 or MOZ), a histone acetyltransferase that acetylates lysine residues on histone H3 to promote an open, transcriptionally permissive chromatin state
Markedly delayed or absent speech is a striking and near-universal feature, often out of proportion to other abilities
Global developmental delay, intellectual disability and infantile hypotonia with feeding difficulties are consistently present
Congenital heart defects, particularly septal defects and patent ductus arteriosus, are common and warrant cardiac assessment
Recurrent infections, gastrointestinal problems and a characteristic facial appearance with a broad nasal tip and small ears support the diagnosis
The genotype influences severity, with truncating variants in certain exons tending to produce a more severe phenotype
As a disorder of a histone acetyltransferase it sits alongside KAT6B-related conditions within the acetyltransferase group of chromatinopathies
reference.pathophysiology: KAT6A encodes a lysine acetyltransferase of the MYST family that transfers acetyl groups onto histone H3, a modification that loosens chromatin structure and facilitates transcription of target genes. Pathogenic variants reduce or distort this acetyltransferase activity, disturbing the acetylation-dependent control of developmental gene expression, including programmes important for neuronal maturation and for cardiac and craniofacial development. The resulting epigenetic dysregulation manifests as intellectual disability with a distinctive speech deficit, hypotonia, congenital heart disease and dysmorphism, and the position and nature of the variant within the gene help explain the observed variation in severity.
additionalDifferentials: Other non-specific syndromic intellectual disability with absent speech
additionalInvestigations: Exome or genome sequencing to identify KAT6A variants
Echocardiography to detect congenital heart defects
Neurodevelopmental assessment with emphasis on expressive language and augmentative communication
Evaluation of feeding and swallowing in infancy
Brain MRI where structural anomalies or seizures are suspected
Immunological assessment if infections are recurrent
redFlags: Significant congenital heart disease requiring cardiological management
Severe feeding difficulty with faltering growth in infancy
Recurrent serious infections suggesting immune vulnerability
reference.prognosis: Life expectancy is not clearly reduced in most, but intellectual disability is typically moderate to severe and expressive speech may remain very limited, so early augmentative and alternative communication and coordinated developmental support are central; cardiac and feeding issues largely determine morbidity in infancy.
pitfalls: Attributing the profound speech delay to isolated language disorder rather than pursuing a genetic diagnosis
Failing to screen for congenital heart disease at diagnosis
Confusing the condition with allelic KAT6B disorders without careful phenotyping and sequencing
Delaying introduction of alternative communication strategies while awaiting speech
references: Nature Reviews — histone acetyltransferases in development and disease
management: Recognise there is no disease-specific therapy, so management is supportive and developmental
Introduce early augmentative and alternative communication and speech-language therapy given the near-universal expressive-speech deficit
Provide multidisciplinary developmental support with physiotherapy and occupational therapy for hypotonia and educational support for intellectual disability
Assess for and manage congenital heart defects such as septal defects and patent ductus arteriosus with cardiology input
Address feeding and swallowing difficulties in infancy with feeding therapy and nutritional support
Monitor for and treat recurrent infections and gastrointestinal problems
Arrange ophthalmological and audiological review with treatment of identified deficits
Offer genetic counselling with recurrence-risk advice, as pathogenic KAT6A variants are typically de novo
